heroHeadline: India Hits 50% Non-Fossil Power 5 Years Early — IRENA Confirms 24/7 Solar+Storage Cheaper Than New Fossil Fuels
heroSubtitle: 3,805 days since the Paris Agreement — India surpassed 50% non-fossil installed electricity capacity in May 2026, five years ahead of its 2030 Paris NDC target, adding a record 55.3 GW in FY 2025–26. IRENA confirmed this week that solar-plus-storage now delivers 24/7 power at $54–$82/MWh in prime markets — below new coal and gas — eliminating the intermittency cost argument against renewables as baseload providers. Ford Energy launched a new US-assembled grid-scale battery storage subsidiary targeting 20 GWh/yr. The Africa Forward Summit in Nairobi produced an 11-point green industrialization declaration and a coalition of 8 nations pushing a luxury air travel levy to raise €187B for climate finance in developing countries.
footerNote: Data sourced from IEA, IRENA, IPCC, UNEP, BloombergNEF, and major international outlets. All figures reflect verified, publicly available data through May 2026.
